## Sampling {#slide-7}

Non-random (convenience) sampling methods are often biased.

Statistics from non-random samples either consistently overestimate or underestimate the true population parameters.

Random sampling

Each unit in the population has an equal probability of being selected for the sample

## Sampling Distributions Activity {#slide-18}

Go to the Sampling Distributions webpage at  http://onlinestatbook.com/stat_sim/sampling_dist/index.html  

Click begin

Steps

Select Normal Distribution for your parent population

Select N = 2

Click animate, click animate again, and again...

Click 10,000

Increase N to 25 and repeat

What do you notice about the mean and standard deviation of your parent population and sampling distributions?

Repeat steps above by changing the parent population to Uniform, Skewed, and Custom

What happens as you change your parent population? What changes as N increases?

## Example 5 {#slide-32}

The television picture tubes of manufacturer  A  have an expected lifetime of 6.5 years and a standard deviation of 0.9 year, while those of manufacturer  B  have an expected lifetime of 6.0 years and a standard deviation of 0.8 year. What is the probability that a random sample of 36 tubes from manufacturer  A  will have a mean lifetime that is at least 1 year more than the mean lifetime of a sample of 49 tubes from manufacturer  B ?

## In-class {#slide-39}

The time (in hours) that a technician requires to perform preventive maintenance on an air-conditioning unit is governed by the exponential distribution with mean 1 hour. Your company has a contract to maintain 70 of these units in an apartment building. You must schedule technicians' time for a visit to this building. Is it safe to budget an average of 1.1 hour for each unit? Or should you budget an average of 1.25 hours?

## Example 8 {#slide-48}

It is known that HW scores follow a normal distribution with mean 80. Given a random sample of 15 HW scores with a sample standard deviation of 5, what is the probability that the average HW score is at least 82?

## Example 9 {#slide-49}

## Example 10 {#slide-50}

An insurance company knows that in the entire population of millions of apartment owners, the mean expected annual loss from damage is \$75 with a standard deviation of \$300. The distribution of losses is strongly right skewed (i.e. most policies have \$0 losses) but a few have large losses. If the company sells 10,000 policies, can it safely base its rates on the assumption that its average loss will be no greater than \$85

## In-class {#slide-51}

It is known that a certain engine is expected to perform at 20 MPG. A random sample of 100 engines is chosen and with the sample variance computed to be 1. Find the probability that, on average, the chosen engines will perform less than 21 MPG.
